cohort: The study included 15 singleton pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia or IUGR (cases) and 17 unaffected singleton pregnancies (controls) managed at St. Michael's Hospital.
finding: Pregnancies complicated by preeclampsia or IUGR had higher uterine artery pulsatility index (UA PI) at 18-22 weeks' gestation than controls, but this difference was not statistically significant by 6 weeks postpartum, suggesting a potential different trajectory for physiologic recovery.
